heading: EXT. WILLOW GROVE AT THE EDGE OF THE WORLD - TWILIGHT

units.text: EXT. WILLOW GROVE AT THE EDGE OF THE WORLD - TWILIGHT
Weeping willows, silver in the dusk.
Fireflies drift between branches like slow sparks.
A pond mirrors a sky with two moons.
A stone well stands among the roots, its lip furred with moss.
A STRANGER walks into the grove: a woman, ageless, barefoot, wrapped in a patchwork cloak that shifts color as she moves.
She carries a lantern with no flame, only a glow like captured dawn.
She stops at the well and sets the lantern on its lip.
I hear you.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: The willows rustle.
A firefly lands on her sleeve, and she watches it breathe.
I know. I know. It's been a long road.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: A voice rises from the well, deep and wet and patient, as though spoken through a thousand years of stone.
Who comes to the Mouth of Names?
units.name: VOICE

units.text: A traveler.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Travelers bear names.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: Mine fell off the road a long way back.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: She kneels.
She dips her hand into the cold dark water.
Ripples spread, and the fireflies pause in the air, holding their light.
Then I shall give you one.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: Give me a good one.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: The water brightens, silver then gold.
When it clears, the surface shows a face: not hers, but a girl's, laughing.
Wren.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: The woman closes her eyes.
The cloak settles to a single color: the deep green of willow leaves.
Wren.
units.name: WREN

units.text: She rises, shoulders loose, as though a weight has slid off.
She picks up the lantern.
Its glow steadies and warms.
Thank you.
units.name: WREN

units.text: Walk well, Wren.
units.name: VOICE

units.text: She leaves the grove.
Behind her, the willows close their branches like curtains.
The fireflies resume their drift, and the two moons climb.
